import sys, json, re, uuid, hashlib, datetime

# THE RECALL PUSH OF ONE MODEL (curator, GH #895). The collector still asks
# memory once per turn -- its fan-in waits for `leg-memory` -- but the QUESTION
# is built here, next to the wall that knows what the conversation is about:
#
#   * `push_ask` (the collector's `recall`, handed on by `./policy` with the
#     two knobs stamped): the ask leaves on `recall` with exactly the hop keys
#     the collector gave it and a richer `recall_query` -- the topic the memory
#     section last named in this session, what the last rounds of the wall
#     named (capitalised words off the sentence start, numbers, dates, quotes;
#     at most eight) and what a short id in the person's words points at, all
#     in front of the person's own words and never more than `recall_budget`
#     characters. Deterministic, no model, one wall read (R-27-11 A).
#     `recall_push` "0" hands the ask on untouched.
#   * `push_gap` (the section `gap` of an answer): a second ask with the gap as
#     its question, marked `gap_ask`, which the parent's edge lifts into context
#     so the answer comes back HERE on `in_gap_bundle` and never to the
#     collector -- the collector has no round for it. Nobody waits on it.
#   * `in_gap_bundle`: a find becomes a `recall` pair in `blocks` and a mark
#     `addendum`; the next ask of the same session hands that pair to
#     `./intake`, the wall's one writer, for its own round -- ahead of the
#     round's first turn -- and marks it `addendum_done`. In a duplex call the find is also said: a section `fact`
#     for the voice model. Nothing found, nothing written.
#
# ONLY WHAT THE ROUND WAS PRESENT FOR LEAVES (GH #925). The question leaves
# the hive -- to the memory, and in the memory pair back into a window -- so
# the topic, the entities and a short id's words in it come from rows that
# pass the audience gate for the round of the ask, and a find is handed only
# to a round that the round of its gap holds; one that does not stays for a
# later round. Every mark written here carries the round that caused it. The
# memory filters its own answer at its own door; this is the gate on what the
# question and the addendum carry.
#
# THE ASK ALWAYS LEAVES. A round whose ask stays here waits for `round_idle_ms`
# with no memory, so every failure on the ask path -- a broken ledger answer, a
# lost park, an exception -- sends the collector's ask as it came.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc.get("body") or {}
envelope = doc.get("envelope") or {}
P = doc.get("params") or {}
header = envelope.get("header") or {}
hop = header.get("hop") or {}
ctx = header.get("context") or {}


# THE AUDIENCE GATE (GH #925). Every row of `wall`, `calls`, `marks`,
# `summaries` and `pins` carries the audience of the round that caused it
# (`audience_set`, a canonical JSON array), and a reader hands a row to a round
# iff the row has one and it names `*` or holds the round as a subset -- the
# affinity rule (templates/affinity/README.md, GH #154/#306). The round is
# `context.audience_set` of the message being served: this hive's edges set
# and delete only `cur_*`, so it rides the context through every ledger round
# trip exactly like `cur_origin`, and it is never guessed from a row. These
# functions are the same text in every cell of this hive that writes or reads
# rows; a lock holds them to one table. Every ledger read asks the store
# first (`round_where`, GH #932), so a hidden row never comes back at all; the
# Python gate stays as the second line behind it.


def audience_of(value):
    """An audience in its canonical form -- a JSON array of strings, sorted,
    no duplicates, no whitespace -- or None when there is none. The round
    arrives as TEXT (a JSON array in a string) and a column comes back as
    text; a list is taken as it is. Absent, empty text, a scalar or
    unparsable text is NOT DECLARED: the empty list is a declared round, None
    is no round at all (affinity `as_set`, GH #306)."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if not value.strip():
            return None
        try:
            value = json.loads(value)
        except ValueError:
            return None
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        return None
    return json.dumps(sorted({str(x) for x in value if str(x)}), separators=(",", ":"))


def allowed(round_value, origin):
    """The gate: a row whose audience is `origin` may reach the round
    `round_value` iff both are declared and the origin names `*` or holds the
    round as a subset. A row from before the rule has no origin and never
    leaves (OR-BD-5); a round nobody declared passes nothing."""
    r, o = audience_of(round_value), audience_of(origin)
    if r is None or o is None:
        return False
    o = set(json.loads(o))
    return "*" in o or set(json.loads(r)) <= o


def passes(row, round_value, session):
    """One reader's verdict on one row. With a declared round it is the gate;
    without one, only a row of the running session that declares no round
    either (or names `*`) passes -- the window and the handover keep a
    round-less conversation going and show nothing from elsewhere (OR-BD-4).
    A row of a declared round never reaches a call nobody declared a round
    for, though it stands in the same session (review M-7: the words of {e,b}
    reached a round-less call of that session, and a round-less recall took
    the addendum of an {e,a} gap). A row that names no session never passes
    a round-less read."""
    if audience_of(round_value) is None:
        if not session or str(row.get("session_id") or "") != session:
            return False
        own = audience_of(row.get("audience_set"))
        return own is not None and (own == "[]" or "*" in json.loads(own))
    return allowed(round_value, row.get("audience_set"))


ROUNDLESS = ["[]", "[\"*\"]"]


def round_where(round_value, session):
    """The store half of the audience gate (GH #932): the `where` terms a
    ledger read adds so that only rows this round may see come back -- page
    bounds, `scanned`, window and renewal sizes and turn counts then hang on
    visible rows alone, and a hidden row costs nothing a reader can count.
    With a declared, non-empty round it is `covers` (the affinity rule in the
    store). Without one -- or with a declared EMPTY round, which `covers`
    refuses -- only rows of the running session that declare no round either
    (`[]`, PP-BD-12) or name `*` come back; a row from before the rule (NULL)
    never does. None: nothing may be read at all (no round and no session).
    The Python gate below stays as the second line."""
    r = audience_of(round_value)
    if r is not None and r != "[]":
        return {"audience_set": {"covers": json.loads(r)}}
    if not session:
        return None
    return {"session_id": session, "audience_set": {"in": list(ROUNDLESS)}}


def audience_meet(values):
    """The audience of a row made of other rows (a summary, a handover
    block): the INTERSECTION of its sources, so it can never be wider than
    any of them (OR-BD-3). A source naming `*` is neutral; one source without
    an audience, or no source at all, makes the result None."""
    out, universal = None, False
    for v in values:
        c = audience_of(v)
        if c is None:
            return None
        s = set(json.loads(c))
        if "*" in s:
            universal = True
            continue
        out = s if out is None else out & s
    if out is None:
        return '["*"]' if universal else None
    return json.dumps(sorted(out), separators=(",", ":"))


FMT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"
ME = "curator-push"
RECALL_TOOL = "memory_recall"
# The hop of the collector's ask, key for key (collector `head` + `recall_ask`).
# What leaves on `recall` carries these and `route`, and nothing else: the
# member's door promotes them and a key it does not know would ride on into the
# memory hive.
ASK_KEYS = ("phase", "turn_id", "session_id", "iter", "recall_query", "memory_tier",
            "recall_window_from", "recall_window_to")
# `recall_budget` when `./policy` stamps none: the memory hive's own
# `query_safe_chars` (memory-hive/recall, GH #88). Above it the hive keeps only
# the last sentence of a query, and an enrichment longer than that would buy
# nothing but the person's last sentence.
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 200
ENTITY_MAX = 8
ENTITY_ROUNDS = 3
WALL_PAGE = 48
REF_MAX = 3
REF_CHARS = 60
# The wall rows read per short id to find one the round may see (GH #925):
# the rows that carry the block come first in hash order; a block said more
# often than this in rows the round may not see is not resolved (fail-closed).
REF_ROWS = 16
# The two sentences of prompt hygiene (R-27-11 B) the talky's own instructions
# carry, as a slot this hive owns: the pack writes the charter, the collector
# the round's mode, and neither is the place for a rule about this window.
HYGIENE_PATH = "instructions.hygiene"
HYGIENE = ("If you are not sure what the person means, or whether something is"
           " true, ask them instead of guessing.")
# The second sentence, said only where the window shows ids (`short_ids`).
HYGIENE_IDS = (" A block in this conversation shows its id as [#<12 hex digits>];"
               " history_read with that id shows the block in full.")
ADDENDUM_FRAME = "[addendum to your last answer -- looked up after it, for: %s]"
NOTHING_PREFIX = "Nothing in this memory answers"
FACT_CHARS = 400
GAP_CHARS = 300
SHORT_ID = re.compile(r"\[?#([0-9a-f]{12})\]?")
# A short id as it leaves toward a reader, in every form the colony makes one
# (OR-KY-81, OR-KY-84): the window's bracket and its forms of a released, a
# shortened and an expired block, a parenthesised one, the bare `#<12..16 hex>`
# a history tool answers with and the full 64-digit block id; one space in
# front taken along, so "a [#..] b" is said as "a b". The pattern is
# `talky/splitter`'s SHORT_ID, byte for byte (GH #894, OR-KY-83) -- that name
# is taken here by the id reader above.
SPOKEN_ID = re.compile(
    r"[ \t]?(?:\[#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}(?: released[^\]\n]{0,64}| expired)?\]"
    r"|\[shortened[^\]\n#]{0,40}#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}[^\]\n]{0,4}\]"
    r"|\(#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}\)"
    r"|(?<![\w#])#(?=[0-9]{0,15}[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}(?!\w)"
    r"|(?<![\w#])#?(?=[0-9]{0,63}[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{64}(?!\w))")
QUOTE = (r'"([^"\n]{2,60})"|„([^“”"\n]{2,60})[“”"]'
         r'|“([^”\n]{2,60})”|«([^»\n]{2,60})»')
DATE = r"(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|\d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}\.(?:\d{2,4})?|\d{1,2}:\d{2})"
NUMBER = r"(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)"
WORD = r"([^\W\d_][\w’'-]*)"
TOKEN = re.compile("(?:%s)|%s|%s|%s" % (QUOTE, DATE, NUMBER, WORD), re.UNICODE)
SENTENCE_GAP = re.compile(r"[.!?:;\n]")
POSSESSIVE = re.compile(r"['’]s$")
# A capital that says nothing about the conversation.
NOT_NAMES = {"i", "i'm", "i'll", "i've", "i'd", "ok", "okay"}

try:
    _MEM
except NameError:
    # A cache of this child's own doing, never the truth (`code` runner mode
    # `resident`): a restarted child starts empty and the ledger read decides.
    _MEM = {"seq": 0, "asks": {}, "gaps": set(), "delivered": set(), "found": set()}
# The RAM guards only catch a message racing its twin inside one child; the
# ledger read is what decides. Bounded, so a long-lived child does not grow.
for _k in ("asks", "gaps", "delivered", "found"):
    if len(_MEM[_k]) > 4096:
        _MEM[_k].clear()


def canonical(value):
    """The one serialisation a block is hashed and stored in: keys sorted,
    UTF-8, no whitespace."""
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def block_hash(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def block_span(text):
    """Where an answer's sidecar block stands: (start, end) or None.

    The boundary is the fence `talky/splitter` cuts (GH #379, #605): the
    ```sidecar fence, or the legacy ```memory fence, to the next closing fence
    or to the end of the text when the completion stopped inside the block.
    Measured, never parsed -- the sections inside are somebody else's business.
    """
    low = text.lower()
    for fence in ("```sidecar", "```memory"):
        at = low.find(fence)
        if at < 0:
            continue
        head = text.find("\n", at)
        close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
        if head >= 0 and close >= 0:
            return at, close + 3
        return at, len(text)
    return None


def stripped_text(text):
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None:
        return text
    return (text[:span[0]] + text[span[1]:]).strip()


def now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(FMT)


def next_seq(n):
    """`n` fresh sequence numbers: microseconds since the epoch like
    `wall.seq`, strictly above anything this child minted before (OR-KY-61)."""
    base = int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000000)
    base = max(base, _MEM["seq"] + 1)
    _MEM["seq"] = base + n - 1
    return [base + i for i in range(n)]


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def park(reason=""):
    if reason:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: %s\n" % reason)
    emit([])


def lstore(ops, phase, call="", reason=""):
    """One message to `./ledger`. Every key the edge reads is always present
    (a failed CEL modifier skips the edge)."""
    return {"header": {"route": "lstore", "phase": phase, "reply_cell": ME,
                       "cur_call": call, "cur_reason": reason},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)} for cid, args in ops]}


def legs(body):
    """The answer of a store message by tool_call id: payload, error code and
    rows affected -- for a bundle (`results[]`) and for a single op alike."""
    out = {}
    for m in body.get("messages") or []:
        if not isinstance(m, dict):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m.get("text") or "null")
        except Exception:
            payload = None
        out[str(m.get("id") or "")] = {"payload": payload, "error_code": "",
                                       "rows_affected": 0}
    results = body.get("results")
    if isinstance(results, list):
        for r in results:
            if not isinstance(r, dict):
                continue
            leg = out.setdefault(str(r.get("tool_call_id") or ""),
                                 {"payload": None, "error_code": "", "rows_affected": 0})
            leg["error_code"] = str(r.get("error_code") or "")
            leg["rows_affected"] = int(r.get("rows_affected") or 0)
    elif len(out) == 1:
        leg = next(iter(out.values()))
        leg["error_code"] = str(hop.get("error_code") or "")
        leg["rows_affected"] = int(hop.get("rows_affected") or 0)
    return out


def rows(lg, cid):
    p = (lg.get(cid) or {}).get("payload")
    return p if isinstance(p, list) else []


def sel(table, columns, where=None, order=None, limit=None):
    a = {"operation": "select", "table": table, "columns": columns}
    if where:
        a["where"] = where
    if order:
        a["order_by"] = [{"col": c, "dir": o} for c, o in order]
    if limit:
        a["limit"] = limit
    return a


def ins(table, row):
    return {"operation": "insert", "table": table, "row": row}


def upd(table, values, where):
    return {"operation": "update", "table": table, "set": values, "where": where}


def report_errors(lg):
    for cid, leg in lg.items():
        if leg["error_code"]:
            sys.stderr.write("curator/push: ledger op %s failed: %s\n" % (cid, leg["error_code"]))


def pending_key(pid):
    return "pending:push:" + pid


def stamped(row, audience, meet=False):
    """A `marks` row with the audience it was caused under (GH #925). A
    round nobody declared writes `[]` (PP-BD-12): a round-less row the
    round-less reads of its own session find in the store (`round_where`),
    where a NULL column would be a row from before the rule that no reader
    hands on (OR-BD-5)."""
    if audience is not None:
        row["audience_set"] = audience
    elif not meet:
        row["audience_set"] = "[]"
    # A `meet` that came out None could not be determined (OR-BD-3): the
    # column stays NULL, a row no reader hands on -- never `[]`, which a
    # round-less read of the session would take.
    return row


def addendum_audience(round_value, gap_audience):
    """The audience of an addendum (OR-BD-3): the meet of the gap's round and
    the round its find came home in. Both round-less (`[]`, PP-BD-12; or the
    gap names `*`) is a round-less addendum, `[]`. One side round-less and the
    other a declared round, or two rounds that share nobody, is NOT a
    round-less row -- it would reach the round-less reads of the session --
    but one nobody may be shown: None."""
    r, g = audience_of(round_value), audience_of(gap_audience)
    if r in (None, "[]"):
        return "[]" if g in ("[]", '["*"]') else None
    if g == "[]":
        return None
    out = audience_meet([r, g])
    return None if out == "[]" else out


def round_read(cid, table, columns, where, order=None, limit=None, session=None):
    """A ledger read for this round (GH #932): `where` with `round_where`
    merged in, as a one-op list -- or no op at all when nothing may be read
    (no round and no session), so the reader finds no rows without a store
    call."""
    rw = round_where(ROUND, session)
    if rw is None:
        return []
    return [(cid, sel(table, columns, dict(where or {}, **rw), order, limit))]


def visible(found, session):
    """The rows of a ledger read the round of this message may be shown or
    asked with (`passes`, GH #925, OR-BD.A.2): with a round, the gate; without
    one, the running session only. A hidden row leaves no trace. The read
    itself already asked the store (`round_read`, GH #932); this is the
    second line."""
    return [r for r in found if isinstance(r, dict) and passes(r, ROUND, session)]


def value_of(row):
    """A mark's `value`: the JSON object it was written as, whether the column
    hands it back as text or already parsed; a bare string stays a string."""
    v = row.get("value")
    if isinstance(v, str):
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(v)
        except ValueError:
            return v
        return parsed
    return v


def knob_on(value):
    """A flag as `./policy` reads one (`flag_of`): empty, "0", "false", "off"
    and "no" are off -- and so is a flag nobody stamped."""
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return value
    return str(value if value is not None else "").strip().lower() not in (
        "", "0", "false", "off", "no")


def knob_budget(value):
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, str) and not value.strip()):
        return DEFAULT_BUDGET
    try:
        return int(float(value))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return DEFAULT_BUDGET


def the_ask(h, body):
    """The collector's ask exactly as it came: its eight keys, empty rather
    than absent (a missing hop key fails the member's promoting modifier), and
    its body."""
    head = {"route": "recall"}
    for k in ASK_KEYS:
        v = h.get(k)
        head[k] = "" if v is None else v
    msgs = body.get("messages")
    return {"header": head, "messages": msgs if isinstance(msgs, list) else []}


def with_query(ask, query):
    out = {"header": dict(ask["header"], recall_query=query),
           "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": query}]}
    return out


# ------------------------------------------------------------ the question

def topic_of(marks):
    """The open topic of this session (OR-KY-71): the name of the newest topic
    mark that carries one, unless an `end` came after it. `./intake` writes a
    mark as the canonical JSON of the memory section's `{movement, name}`; a
    bare string is a movement and names nothing."""
    for r in marks:
        v = value_of(r)
        if isinstance(v, dict):
            movement = str(v.get("movement") or "").strip().lower()
            name = str(v.get("name") or "").strip()
        else:
            movement, name = str(v or "").strip().lower(), ""
        if movement == "end":
            return ""
        if name:
            return name
    return ""


def recent_rounds(wall):
    """The participant rows of the newest `ENTITY_ROUNDS` rounds of the wall
    (newest first): the person's and a peer's turns and the model's final
    answers -- an interim sentence beside a tool call says nothing new."""
    keys, out = [], []
    for r in wall:
        key = (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""))
        kind = str(r.get("kind") or "")
        if kind == "assistant" and int(r.get("final") or 0) != 1:
            continue
        if kind not in ("user", "peer", "assistant"):
            continue
        if key not in keys:
            if len(keys) >= ENTITY_ROUNDS:
                break
            keys.append(key)
        out.append(r)
    return out


def entities(texts, skip):
    """The fixed heuristic of R-27-11 A (OR-KY-P1): in each text, in order,
    quotes, dates, numbers, and words that start with a capital where no
    sentence starts. Newest text first, each once, at most `ENTITY_MAX`, none
    the person already said."""
    seen, out = set(skip), []
    for text in texts:
        prev = None
        for m in TOKEN.finditer(text):
            quoted = next((g for g in m.groups()[:4] if g), None)
            date, number, word = m.group(5), m.group(6), m.group(7)
            # A sentence starts at the text's first token and after a stop or
            # a line break -- what lies BETWEEN two tokens says so.
            at_start = prev is None or bool(SENTENCE_GAP.search(text[prev:m.start()]))
            prev = m.end()
            item = ""
            if quoted:
                item = quoted.strip()
            elif date:
                item = date
            elif number:
                item = number
            elif word and word[0].isupper() and not at_start:
                word = POSSESSIVE.sub("", word).rstrip("-'’")
                if len(word) < 2 or word.lower() in NOT_NAMES or word.lower().startswith("i'"):
                    continue
                item = word
            if not item or item.lower() in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(item.lower())
            out.append(item)
            if len(out) >= ENTITY_MAX:
                return out
    return out


def compose(user_text, topic, found, refs, budget):
    """The query: what the wall knows, in front of the person's own words, and
    never more than `budget` characters. The person's words are never cut --
    the memory hive's own hygiene guard is the one place a question is cut
    (GH #88) -- and they come LAST, because that guard and its keyword cap
    both keep the tail of a query."""
    parts = []
    if topic:
        parts.append("topic: " + topic)
    if found:
        parts.append("mentioned: " + ", ".join(found))
    for r in refs:
        parts.append("refers to: " + r)
    if budget <= 0 or len(user_text) >= budget:
        return user_text
    room = budget - len(user_text) - 1
    kept = []
    for p in parts:
        piece = "; ".join(kept + [p])
        if len(piece) + 2 > room:
            if p.startswith("mentioned: "):
                # Fewer entities rather than none: drop from the oldest end.
                names = list(found)
                while names:
                    names.pop()
                    trial = "; ".join(kept + ["mentioned: " + ", ".join(names)])
                    if names and len(trial) + 2 <= room:
                        kept.append("mentioned: " + ", ".join(names))
                        break
            continue
        kept.append(p)
    if not kept:
        return user_text
    return "[" + "; ".join(kept) + "] " + user_text


def element_text(body):
    try:
        el = json.loads(str(body or ""))
    except ValueError:
        return ""
    return str(el.get("text") or "") if isinstance(el, dict) else ""


# ------------------------------------------------------------ the addendum

def addendum_pair(gap, text):
    """The pair a find is shown as (OR-KY-P3): a `memory_recall` call with the
    gap as its question and the find as its result, framed as an addendum.
    The id is derived, so the same find for the same gap is the same pair --
    the same hash, and a pair the window already carries is not carried twice."""
    cid = "call_addendum_" + hashlib.sha256(
        ("%s\x1f%s" % (gap, text)).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    call = {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
            "text": json.dumps({"name": RECALL_TOOL,
                                "arguments": json.dumps({"query": gap})})}
    result = {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": cid,
              "text": (ADDENDUM_FRAME % gap) + "\n" + text}
    return call, result


def bundle_find(body, h):
    """The readable text of a gap's bundle, or "" when memory had nothing: an
    empty bundle says so on its hop (`recall_empty`, #297), a refusal comes as
    a reject (`reject_reason`), and the empty-state sentence is not a find."""
    if str(h.get("recall_empty") or "") == "1" or str(h.get("reject_reason") or ""):
        return ""
    text = ""
    for m in body.get("messages") or []:
        if isinstance(m, dict) and str(m.get("text") or "").strip():
            text = str(m.get("text") or "").strip()
    if not text or text.startswith(NOTHING_PREFIX):
        return ""
    return text


def unmarked(text):
    """`text` without the short block ids it quotes, in the splitter's form
    (GH #894): an id at the very start takes the space behind it along."""
    out = SPOKEN_ID.sub("", text)
    if out == text:
        return text
    return out.lstrip(" \t") if SPOKEN_ID.match(text) else out


def said_aloud(gap, text):
    """A find as the voice model hears it: one plain paragraph, and no short
    block id in it. The `fact` leaves the colony -- the member hands it to the
    channel as advice and the voice reads it out -- and R-27-3 keeps internal
    ids inside (OR-KY-68). Both halves can carry one: the gap section passes
    the splitter's filter on purpose (the curator's sections keep their ids),
    and a model with `short_ids` on writes "whether [#0123456789ab] ..." there;
    a find quotes episodes of earlier answers as the tap filed them. The
    window's addendum keeps the ids: the model reads it, and `history_read`
    takes them (review I-2)."""
    flat = unmarked(" ".join(line.strip(" -*\t") for line in text.splitlines()
                             if line.strip()))
    if len(flat) > FACT_CHARS:
        flat = flat[:FACT_CHARS].rsplit(" ", 1)[0] + " ..."
    return "Addendum to what was just said (%s): %s" % (unmarked(gap), flat)


# ======================================================================= LANES
# The round this message serves, read here at every step (OR-BD.A.1): the
# context rides every ledger round trip of this hive, and a gap's ask out of
# the hive and its answer home. Never read off a row.
ROUND = ctx.get("audience_set")
AUD = audience_of(ROUND)
lane = str(hop.get("route") or "")
phase = str(ctx.get("cur_phase") or "")
op = str(hop.get("operation") or "")

if lane == "push_ask":
    ask = the_ask(hop, d)
    try:
        if not knob_on(hop.get("recall_push")):
            emit([ask])
        budget = knob_budget(hop.get("recall_budget"))
        pid = str(uuid.uuid4())
        # The session as `./intake` keys it (R-KX-2): none named is "default".
        session = str(ask["header"].get("session_id") or "default")
        stash = {"ask": ask, "budget": budget, "short": knob_on(hop.get("short_ids"))}
        _MEM["asks"][pid] = ask
        # The topic, the addenda and the wall page are read with their
        # audience: each goes into what leaves the hive only if it passes the
        # gate for this round (GH #925).
        # The topic, the addenda, the wall page and the summary cover ask the
        # store for this round's rows only (GH #932): the page of `WALL_PAGE`
        # and the topic page fill with rows the round may see, and a hidden
        # row costs none of their places.
        ops = [("a-put", ins("state", {"key": pending_key(pid), "value": canonical(stash)})),
               ("a-echo", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": pending_key(pid)}))]
        # Every quiet turn leaves a nameless `continue` (the nothing form);
        # those carry nothing and would push a named mark out of the page.
        ops += round_read("a-topic", "marks", ["seq", "session_id", "value", "audience_set"],
                          {"session_id": session, "kind": "topic",
                           "value": {"neq": canonical({"movement": "continue", "name": ""})}},
                          [("seq", "desc")], 16, session)
        ops += round_read("a-add", "marks", ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "kind", "value",
                                             "audience_set"],
                          {"session_id": session, "kind": "addendum"},
                          [("seq", "asc")], None, session)
        # Which finds were handed on is bookkeeping for a write (whether an
        # `addendum_done` is due), read whole: it only holds a visible find
        # back, and nothing of it leaves.
        ops.append(("a-done", sel("marks", ["seq", "kind", "value"],
                                  {"session_id": session, "kind": "addendum_done"},
                                  [("seq", "asc")])))
        ops += round_read("a-wall", "wall", ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "kind", "hash",
                                             "final", "audience_set"],
                          {"kind": {"in": ["user", "peer", "assistant"]}},
                          [("seq", "desc")], WALL_PAGE, session)
        ops += [("a-state", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": "push:tier"})),
                ("a-slot", sel("slots", ["path", "hash", "owner"], {"path": HYGIENE_PATH}))]
        # The newest summary THIS round may see bounds its window; summaries
        # name no session, so a round-less ask reads none (cover 0).
        ops += round_read("a-cover", "summaries", ["covers_to_seq"], None,
                          [("covers_to_seq", "desc")], 1)
        emit([lstore(ops, "ask", pid)])
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: ask not enriched (%s) -- sent as it came\n" % exc)
        emit([ask])

if lane == "push_gap":
    # The splitter hands a string on as `{payload: <text>}`; a model that wrote
    # the section as an object gets its words read in order -- one gap, one
    # mark, whatever form it came in.
    payload = d.get("payload")
    if isinstance(payload, dict) and ("payload" in payload or "text" in payload):
        gap = payload.get("payload", payload.get("text", ""))
    elif isinstance(payload, dict):
        gap = " ".join(str(v) for v in payload.values() if isinstance(v, (str, int, float)))
    else:
        gap = payload
    gap = " ".join(str(gap or "").split())[:GAP_CHARS]
    if not gap:
        park("a gap section without words -- nothing to look up")
    session = str(ctx.get("session_id") or hop.get("session_id") or "default")
    turn = str(ctx.get("turn_id") or hop.get("turn_id") or "")
    gid = hashlib.sha256(("%s\x1f%s\x1f%s" % (session, turn, gap)).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    if gid in _MEM["gaps"]:
        park("gap %s is already being looked up" % gid)
    _MEM["gaps"].add(gid)
    info = {"id": gid, "text": gap, "engine": str(ctx.get("engine") or ""),
            "on": "1" if knob_on(hop.get("recall_push")) else "0",
            "budget": knob_budget(hop.get("recall_budget")),
            "iter": str(ctx.get("iter") or hop.get("iter") or "0")}
    ops = [("g-marks", sel("marks", ["value"],
                           {"session_id": session, "turn_id": turn, "kind": "gap"})),
           ("g-state", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": "push:tier"}))]
    emit([lstore(ops, "gap", gid, canonical(info))])

if lane == "in_gap_bundle":
    gid = str(ctx.get("gap_ask") or "")
    found = bundle_find(d, hop)
    if not gid:
        park("a gap bundle without its gap_ask -- dropped")
    if not found:
        park("gap %s: memory had nothing -- no addendum" % gid)
    if gid in _MEM["found"]:
        park("gap %s: its find is already kept" % gid)
    _MEM["found"].add(gid)
    session = str(ctx.get("session_id") or "default")
    pid = "gap-" + gid
    ops = [("h-put", ins("state", {"key": pending_key(pid), "value": canonical({"text": found})})),
           ("h-echo", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": pending_key(pid)})),
           ("h-marks", sel("marks", ["turn_id", "kind", "value", "audience_set"],
                           {"session_id": session, "kind": {"in": ["gap", "addendum"]}}))]
    emit([lstore(ops, "hit", pid, session)])

if lane:
    park("unknown lane %r -- dropped" % lane)

# ================================================================= PHASES
if not op:
    park("a message with neither a lane nor a store answer -- dropped")

lg = legs(d)
call = str(ctx.get("cur_call") or "")
reason = str(ctx.get("cur_reason") or "")

if phase == "done":
    report_errors(lg)
    emit([])

if phase == "ask":
    # The ask is the one thing this phase must never lose.
    try:
        echo = rows(lg, "a-echo")
        stash = json.loads(str(echo[0].get("value") or "{}")) if echo else {}
    except (ValueError, AttributeError, IndexError):
        stash = {}
    ask = stash.get("ask") or _MEM["asks"].get(call)
    if not ask:
        park("ask %s lost its park -- the round waits for its idle window" % call)
    try:
        report_errors(lg)
        head = ask["header"]
        # The session as the lane keyed its reads (R-KX-2).
        session = str(head.get("session_id") or "default")
        text = str(head.get("recall_query") or "")
        # GH #925: the topic and the rows the entities come from are the ones
        # this round may be asked with -- a round that was not present when a
        # topic was named, or a row was said, is not asked with it.
        topic = topic_of(visible(rows(lg, "a-topic"), session))
        recent = recent_rounds(visible(rows(lg, "a-wall"), session))
        # Which finds were handed on is bookkeeping, read whole (`a-done`).
        done = {str((value_of(r) or {}).get("id") or "") for r in rows(lg, "a-done")
                if r.get("kind") == "addendum_done" and isinstance(value_of(r), dict)}
        pend = []
        for r in rows(lg, "a-add"):
            v = value_of(r)
            if r.get("kind") != "addendum" or not isinstance(v, dict):
                continue
            aid = str(v.get("id") or "")
            if not aid or aid in done or aid in _MEM["delivered"] or aid in [p["id"] for p in pend]:
                continue
            # A find is handed only to a round the round of its gap holds; one
            # it does not stays, undone, for a later round that may see it.
            if not passes(r, ROUND, session):
                continue
            pend.append({"id": aid, "call": str(v.get("call") or ""),
                         "result": str(v.get("result") or "")})
        covers = rows(lg, "a-cover")
        cover = int(covers[0].get("covers_to_seq") or 0) if covers else 0
        tier = {str(r.get("key")): str(r.get("value") or "") for r in rows(lg, "a-state")}
        slot = (rows(lg, "a-slot") or [None])[0]
        refs = []
        for m in SHORT_ID.finditer(text):
            if m.group(1) not in refs:
                refs.append(m.group(1))
        refs = refs[:REF_MAX]
        needed = sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in recent}
                        | {p["call"] for p in pend} | {p["result"] for p in pend})
        slim = {"ask": ask, "budget": stash.get("budget", DEFAULT_BUDGET), "topic": topic,
                "short": bool(stash.get("short")),
                "recent": [{"hash": str(r.get("hash") or ""), "kind": str(r.get("kind") or "")}
                           for r in recent],
                "pending": pend, "refs": refs,
                "tier": tier.get("push:tier"), "has_tier": "push:tier" in tier,
                "slot": slot}
        ops = [("b-slim", upd("state", {"value": canonical(slim)}, {"key": pending_key(call)})),
               ("b-echo", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": pending_key(call)}))]
        if needed:
            ops.append(("b-blocks", sel("blocks", ["hash", "kind", "body"],
                                        {"hash": {"in": [h for h in needed if h]}})))
        if pend:
            # "In the window" is in the window of THIS round: a row it may not
            # see neither shows the pair nor keeps it back (GH #925).
            ops += round_read("b-seen", "wall", ["hash", "session_id", "audience_set"],
                              {"seq": {"gt": cover},
                               "hash": {"in": sorted({p["result"] for p in pend})}},
                              None, None, session)
        for i, ref in enumerate(refs):
            ops.append(("b-ref%d" % i, sel("blocks", ["hash", "body"], {"hash": {"gte": ref}},
                                           [("hash", "asc")], 1)))
            # The wall rows that carry the block, first in hash order: a short
            # id is resolved only where the round may see one of them -- an id
            # copied out of another conversation names nothing (GH #925). The
            # store hands back only rows the round may see (GH #932), so
            # `REF_ROWS` counts those alone.
            ops += round_read("b-refw%d" % i, "wall", ["hash", "session_id", "audience_set"],
                              {"hash": {"gte": ref}},
                              [("hash", "asc"), ("seq", "desc")], REF_ROWS, session)
        emit([lstore(ops, "ask-b", call)])
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: ask %s not enriched (%s) -- sent as it came\n"
                         % (call, exc))
        _MEM["asks"].pop(call, None)
        emit([lstore([("x-drop", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                                  "where": {"key": pending_key(call)}})], "done", call), ask])

if phase == "ask-b":
    try:
        echo = rows(lg, "b-echo")
        slim = json.loads(str(echo[0].get("value") or "{}")) if echo else {}
    except (ValueError, AttributeError, IndexError):
        slim = {}
    ask = slim.get("ask") or _MEM["asks"].get(call)
    drop = ("c-drop", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                       "where": {"key": pending_key(call)}})
    if not ask:
        park("ask %s lost its park -- the round waits for its idle window" % call)
    _MEM["asks"].pop(call, None)
    try:
        report_errors(lg)
        head = ask["header"]
        session = str(head.get("session_id") or "default")
        turn = str(head.get("turn_id") or "")
        text = str(head.get("recall_query") or "")
        blocks = {}
        for r in rows(lg, "b-blocks"):
            blocks.setdefault(str(r.get("hash") or ""), r)
        texts = []
        for r in slim.get("recent") or []:
            b = blocks.get(r.get("hash"))
            if b is not None:
                texts.append(stripped_text(element_text(b.get("body"))))
        found = entities([t for t in texts if t], {w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"\w+", text)})
        refs = []
        for i, ref in enumerate(slim.get("refs") or []):
            seen_by = {str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in visible(rows(lg, "b-refw%d" % i), session)}
            for r in rows(lg, "b-ref%d" % i):
                h_ = str(r.get("hash") or "")
                if h_.startswith(ref) and h_ in seen_by:
                    snip = " ".join(stripped_text(element_text(r.get("body"))).split())
                    if snip:
                        refs.append(snip[:REF_CHARS])
        query = compose(text, str(slim.get("topic") or ""), found, refs,
                        int(slim.get("budget") or DEFAULT_BUDGET))
        out = with_query(ask, query)
        stamp = now()
        ops = []
        # The memory tier the ambient leg of this surface asks with: a gap is
        # looked up at the same tier, and only where an ambient leg exists.
        tier = str(head.get("memory_tier") or "")
        if not slim.get("has_tier"):
            ops.append(("c-tier", ins("state", {"key": "push:tier", "value": tier})))
        elif slim.get("tier") != tier:
            ops.append(("c-tier", upd("state", {"value": tier}, {"key": "push:tier"})))
        # Prompt hygiene: the slot is this hive's, written once and again only
        # when its words change.
        slot = slim.get("slot")
        words = HYGIENE + (HYGIENE_IDS if slim.get("short") else "")
        el = {"path": HYGIENE_PATH, "text": words}
        sh = block_hash(el)
        if not isinstance(slot, dict) or str(slot.get("hash") or "") != sh:
            ops.append(("c-hb", ins("blocks", {"hash": sh, "kind": "system", "chars": len(words),
                                               "body": canonical(el), "first_seen": stamp})))
            if isinstance(slot, dict):
                ops.append(("c-hs", upd("slots", {"hash": sh, "owner": "curator", "at": stamp},
                                        {"path": HYGIENE_PATH})))
            else:
                ops.append(("c-hs", ins("slots", {"path": HYGIENE_PATH, "hash": sh,
                                                  "owner": "curator", "at": stamp})))
        # The addenda: for THIS round, ahead of its first turn. The pair goes to
        # `./intake`, the wall's one writer (OR-KX.K.1), before the ask leaves
        # the hive -- the round itself comes in only after the memory answered.
        # A pair whose result the window already carries is not carried twice.
        seen = {str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in visible(rows(lg, "b-seen"), session)}
        pair, rows_out = [], []
        for p in slim.get("pending") or []:
            cb, rb = blocks.get(p["call"]), blocks.get(p["result"])
            why = ""
            if p["result"] in seen:
                why = "in the window"
            elif cb is None or rb is None:
                why = "its blocks are gone"
            else:
                pair += [json.loads(str(cb.get("body") or "{}")),
                         json.loads(str(rb.get("body") or "{}"))]
            # Two finds of one pair in one round are one block, shown once.
            seen.add(p["result"])
            _MEM["delivered"].add(p["id"])
            rows_out.append((p, why))
        for (p, why), seq in zip(rows_out, next_seq(len(rows_out)) if rows_out else []):
            ops.append(("c-m%d" % seq, ins("marks", stamped({
                "seq": seq, "session_id": session, "turn_id": turn,
                "kind": "addendum_done",
                "value": canonical({"id": p["id"], "delivered": 0 if why else 1,
                                    "why": why}), "at": stamp}, AUD))))
        ops.append(drop)
        shown = [{"header": {"route": "in_addendum", "session_id": session, "turn_id": turn},
                  "messages": pair}] if pair else []
        emit([lstore(ops, "done", call)] + shown + [out])
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: ask %s not enriched (%s) -- sent as it came\n"
                         % (call, exc))
        emit([lstore([drop], "done", call), ask])

if phase == "gap":
    report_errors(lg)
    try:
        info = json.loads(reason or "{}")
    except ValueError:
        park("gap %s lost what it asked -- dropped" % call)
    session = str(ctx.get("session_id") or hop.get("session_id") or "default")
    turn = str(ctx.get("turn_id") or hop.get("turn_id") or "")
    for r in rows(lg, "g-marks"):
        v = value_of(r)
        if isinstance(v, dict) and str(v.get("id") or "") == call:
            park("gap %s is already on the record -- not looked up twice" % call)
    state = {str(r.get("key")): str(r.get("value") or "") for r in rows(lg, "g-state")}
    tier = state.get("push:tier", "")
    searched = info.get("on") == "1" and bool(tier)
    stamp = now()
    seq = next_seq(1)[0]
    # The round of the answer that named the gap; it also rides the gap's own
    # ask out and its answer home, in the context.
    mark = ins("marks", stamped({"seq": seq, "session_id": session, "turn_id": turn,
                                 "kind": "gap",
                                 "value": canonical({"id": call, "text": info.get("text", ""),
                                                     "engine": info.get("engine", ""),
                                                     "searched": 1 if searched else 0}),
                                 "at": stamp}, AUD))
    out = [lstore([("g-mark", mark)], "done", call)]
    if searched:
        # The second ask: the gap is its question, at the tier of this
        # surface's ambient leg, under the gap's own round -- and `gap_ask`,
        # which the parent's edge lifts into context so the answer finds its
        # way back here instead of into the collector.
        head = {"route": "recall", "phase": "recall", "turn_id": turn, "session_id": session,
                "iter": str(info.get("iter") or "0"),
                "recall_query": str(info.get("text") or "")[:max(int(info.get("budget") or 0),
                                                                  DEFAULT_BUDGET)],
                "memory_tier": tier, "recall_window_from": "", "recall_window_to": "",
                "gap_ask": call}
        out.append({"header": head,
                    "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text",
                                  "text": head["recall_query"]}]})
    else:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: gap %s kept, not looked up (%s)\n"
                         % (call, "recall_push off" if info.get("on") != "1"
                            else "this surface asks memory on no turn"))
    emit(out)

if phase == "hit":
    report_errors(lg)
    gid = call[len("gap-"):] if call.startswith("gap-") else call
    session = reason
    echo = rows(lg, "h-echo")
    try:
        found = str(json.loads(str(echo[0].get("value") or "{}")).get("text") or "") if echo else ""
    except ValueError:
        found = ""
    gap_row, known = None, False
    for r in rows(lg, "h-marks"):
        v = value_of(r)
        if not isinstance(v, dict) or str(v.get("id") or "") != gid:
            continue
        if r.get("kind") == "gap":
            gap_row = (r, v)
        elif r.get("kind") == "addendum":
            known = True
    drop = ("i-drop", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                       "where": {"key": pending_key(call)}})
    if not found or gap_row is None or known:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: gap %s: %s -- no addendum\n"
                         % (gid, "its find is gone" if not found else
                            "no gap on the record" if gap_row is None else
                            "the addendum is already kept"))
        emit([lstore([drop], "done", call)])
    r, v = gap_row
    gap = str(v.get("text") or "")
    c_el, r_el = addendum_pair(gap, found)
    # The addendum is made of two texts: the gap, said in the round of its
    # answer, and the find, looked up in the round this answer came home in --
    # the same round, which rode the gap's ask out and back in the context.
    # Its audience is the meet of both (OR-BD-3), never wider than either.
    stash = {"gap": gap, "text": found, "turn": str(r.get("turn_id") or ""),
             "engine": str(v.get("engine") or ""), "session": session,
             "call": block_hash(c_el), "result": block_hash(r_el),
             "audience": addendum_audience(ROUND, r.get("audience_set"))}
    # `h-marks` is read whole: a lookup by the gap's id for this write (the
    # gap's words, and whether the addendum is already kept). What it finds
    # leaves only inside the addendum, under the meet above (GH #932).
    ops = [("j-put", upd("state", {"value": canonical(stash)}, {"key": pending_key(call)})),
           ("j-echo", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": pending_key(call)})),
           ("j-blocks", sel("blocks", ["hash"], {"hash": {"in": sorted({stash["call"],
                                                                        stash["result"]})}}))]
    if stash["engine"] == "duplex":
        # The round on the line NOW: that of the session's newest call, read in
        # this bundle (no round trip more) -- a duplex find is spoken at once.
        # Read whole on purpose (GH #932): it asks WHO listens now, not what
        # this round may see -- filtered by this round, a newer call the round
        # does not cover would hide behind an older one and the find would be
        # said to a round that may not hear it. Only `allowed` reads it.
        ops.append(("j-now", sel("calls", ["audience_set"], {"session_id": session},
                                 [("started_at", "desc")], 1)))
    emit([lstore(ops, "keep", call, session)])

if phase == "keep":
    report_errors(lg)
    gid = call[len("gap-"):] if call.startswith("gap-") else call
    echo = rows(lg, "j-echo")
    try:
        st = json.loads(str(echo[0].get("value") or "{}")) if echo else {}
    except ValueError:
        st = {}
    drop = ("k-drop", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                       "where": {"key": pending_key(call)}})
    if not st.get("text"):
        park("gap %s lost its find -- no addendum" % gid)
    have = {str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in rows(lg, "j-blocks")}
    c_el, r_el = addendum_pair(st["gap"], st["text"])
    stamp = now()
    ops = []
    for i, (el, h) in enumerate(((c_el, st["call"]), (r_el, st["result"]))):
        if h not in have:
            ops.append(("k-b%d" % i, ins("blocks", {"hash": h, "kind": "recall",
                                                    "chars": len(str(el.get("text") or "")),
                                                    "body": canonical(el),
                                                    "first_seen": stamp})))
    seq = next_seq(1)[0]
    ops.append(("k-mark", ins("marks", stamped({
        "seq": seq, "session_id": st["session"], "turn_id": st["turn"], "kind": "addendum",
        "value": canonical({"id": gid, "call": st["call"], "result": st["result"],
                            "gap": st["gap"]}), "at": stamp}, st.get("audience"), meet=True))))
    ops.append(drop)
    out = [lstore(ops, "done", call)]
    live = (rows(lg, "j-now") or [{}])[0].get("audience_set")
    if st.get("engine") == "duplex" and allowed(live, st.get("audience")):
        # A duplex call has no next round of this model to wait for: the voice
        # model is speaking now, so the find goes to it as a `fact` as well --
        # only when the round on the line now may see it (review M-10,
        # R2-I-14): the gap's round rode the ask out and home, and someone
        # may have joined the call since. Kept as an addendum all the same.
        out.append({"header": {"route": "sidecar", "section": "fact"}, "messages": [],
                    "section": "fact", "payload": {"payload": said_aloud(st["gap"], st["text"])}})
    elif st.get("engine") == "duplex":
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: gap %s: the round on the line may not hear its find"
                         " -- no fact, the addendum is kept (GH #925)\n" % gid)
    emit(out)

park("store answer in unknown phase %r -- dropped" % phase)

description.purpose: The recall push of one model (GH #895). It builds the question of the collector's per-turn memory ask out of the wall -- the topic the memory section last named in the session, what the last three rounds named, what a short id in the person's words points at -- in front of the person's own words and within `recall_budget`, and hands the ask on with exactly the collector's hop keys. It looks a `gap` of an answer up after the answer, keeps a find as a `recall` pair and an `addendum` mark, and hands that pair to `./intake`, the wall's one writer, for the session's next round, ahead of its first turn; in a duplex call it also sends the find as a `fact` for the voice model.
description.use_when: Inside the curator only, behind `./policy`, which stamps the knobs `recall_push`, `recall_budget` and `short_ids` -- as the role resolved them -- on both of its doors.
description.not_in_scope: No model call and no retrieval of its own: memory answers, this cell only asks. An ask that cannot be enriched leaves as it came -- the collector's fan-in waits for it.
description.emits_meaning: recall: the ask, with the collector's keys (plus `gap_ask` on a gap's own ask). sidecar: a gap's find as a section `fact`, duplex calls only. lstore: ledger operations. in_addendum: a find's pair for `./intake`, which writes it into the wall of the round it opens.
description.consumes_meaning: push_ask and push_gap from `./policy`, in_gap_bundle from outside (the answer to a gap's ask), and the ledger's answers to its phases (ask, ask-b, gap, hit, keep, done).
